title: Data-Structure Design

views.title: Data-Structure Design
views.intro: The pattern is almost always a hash map for lookup plus an ordering structure (linked list, TreeMap, heap, array with swap-delete) that makes the second operation cheap. State the complexity of every operation before coding.
table: Map + doubly linked list; frequency buckets with minFreq
Array + index map, swap with last on delete
Per-user lists merged with a heap
Deque of timestamps, token bucket, circular buckets

files.desc: LRU (hand-rolled and LinkedHashMap), LFU, randomized set, max stack, Twitter feed, rate limiter, token bucket, snapshot array, hit counter, peeking iterator, consistent hashing

pitfalls: LRU: use sentinel head and tail nodes so no operation needs null checks.
LFU: when the min-frequency bucket empties during a touch, increment minFreq; on insert, reset it to 1.
Say aloud which operations are O(1) and which are O(log n) and why.

decisions.q: Evict least frequently used, ties by recency?
decisions.a: freq to LinkedHashSet buckets, track minFreq
Heap over each user's newest tweet
Deque of timestamps or token bucket

decisions.q: Route keys to nodes with minimal remapping?

calibration: SDE2 bar: LRU cache, min stack, insert/delete/getRandom O(1), implement a queue with stacks.
SDE3 bar: LFU cache, Twitter feed, max stack, time-based key-value store, rate limiter, snapshot array, iterator designs.
Staff bar (for context): thread-safety discussion for these structures, sharding and consistent hashing, and trade-offs between exact and approximate counters.
